title: A+ eligibility and purpose
source: Amazon Seller Central - A+ content guidelines
do: Confirm Brand Registry enrolment, then use A+ to replace the plain description with brand story, comparison and lifestyle modules.
dont: Do not plan A+ for a reseller listing that does not own the brand, and do not repeat the bullets verbatim inside the modules.
why: A+ requires Brand Registry and its job is persuasion the bullets cannot carry.

title: A+ comparison table
do: Use the comparison table to differentiate variants or sibling products on the attributes buyers actually compare.
dont: Do not compare against competitor brands or make claims you cannot substantiate.
why: Comparison tables work as an in-page decision aid; competitor comparisons create policy risk.

title: A+ image and text limits
source: Amazon Seller Central - A+ module specifications
do: Meet each module's image dimensions and text limits, and keep text legible on mobile.
dont: Do not stretch images, exceed the character limits, or bake essential text into an image only.
why: Modules that break the spec get rejected, and text inside images is invisible to search and accessibility.

title: A+ and ads together
source: Amazon Ads - conversion and A+ guidance
do: Publish A+ before scaling ads, then judge the ad impact only after the A+ page is live.
dont: Do not scale spend on a bare listing and blame the ads for a low conversion rate.
why: Conversion rate sets the ACOS a campaign can sustain; A+ lifts conversion on the same traffic.

title: Invoice requirements for gating
do: Keep supplier invoices that show the brand, the quantity purchased and a date inside the requested window.
dont: Do not submit retail receipts, order confirmations or screenshots as proof of authenticity.
why: Gating reviews reject retail documentation, and a failed review can block the category.

title: Condition grading
do: Grade the item from its real state and use the standard grades such as Used - Like New or Used - Very Good.
dont: Do not list opened, tested or customer-returned units as New to win the Buy Box.
why: Condition mismatches drive returns, negative feedback and account-health warnings.

title: Store pages need a reason
do: Give every Store page one job: a product family, a use case, or a brand story, with one clear next click.
dont: Do not build a Store page as a wall of every SKU with no hierarchy.
why: Stores convert when the page answers a single question; a flat catalogue wastes the visit.

title: Brand story and trust
source: Amazon Seller Central - brand story module
do: Use the brand story module to state who makes the product, where, and what standard it meets.
dont: Do not use unverifiable superlatives or badges the brand has not earned.
why: Provenance and standards are what differentiate a private label from a commodity listing.

title: Listing image order
do: Lead with the clean product on white, then use images 2 to 6 for scale, use case, detail and packaging.
dont: Do not spend the second image on a logo or a lifestyle shot that repeats the first.
why: Buyers swipe for information; each slot should answer a different objection.

title: Video for listings
do: Keep the listing video short, show the product in use, and keep any on-screen text legible on a phone.
dont: Do not reuse a 60 second brand film as the listing video or claim results the product cannot prove.
why: Listing video is a decision aid watched on mobile, not a brand advertisement.

title: Feed before bids
do: Clear Merchant Center disapprovals and missing attributes before changing bids or budgets.
dont: Do not add budget to a campaign whose products are disapproved or whose feed is incomplete.
why: A disapproved product cannot serve, so spend changes have no effect until the feed is fixed.

title: Brand traffic separation
source: Google Ads - brand and Performance Max
do: Run a separate brand search campaign and exclude brand terms from Performance Max where the account allows it.
dont: Do not report Performance Max return as incremental when it is harvesting existing brand demand.
why: Brand searches convert at a high rate regardless of the campaign, so blending them inflates reported performance.
